messages:
joel: Heads-up: users on Windows + CPython 3.11 hitting intermittent TLS handshake errors with the Python SDK when talking to our private load balancer. Error snippet:

requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER] wrong version number (_ssl.c:1123)

Only reproducible on some Windows boxes (esp. older Win10 builds). Works fine on linux and mac. Anyone seen this pattern?

erin: Could be a proxy or TLSv1.3 negotiation mismatch. Can you dump OpenSSL version: `python -c "import ssl; print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)"` and also check requests + urllib3 versions? Windows Pythons sometimes bundle an older OpenSSL or ship behind a custom schannel behavior.

joel: OpenSSL shows OpenSSL 1.1.1k  FIPS, requests 2.31.0, urllib3 2.0.4. We tested by curling the host from the same machine and curl succeeds. This looks specific to Python TLS stack.

marta: Two related notes from previous incidents: 1) pip installing from sdist on Windows can compile against system OpenSSL (mismatched CA behavior). 2) Some windows builds prefer schannel which behaves differently than OpenSSL. For cert trust we previously recommended `python-certifi-win32` but that won't fix version negotiation.

erin: Quick diagnostic: try forcing TLSv1.2 in a small script to see if negotiation fallback stops the error:

```
import ssl, requests
ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLSv1_2)
resp = requests.get('https://api.staging.redwood', verify=ctx)
```

If that works, we can fallback in SDK for affected Windows+py combos. Not ideal but useful until we ship wheels.

joel: Forcing TLSv1_2 made the call succeed. Also saw differences when starting Python from Git Bash vs cmd.exe (maybe different CA path).

marta: Actionable things: short-term: add REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE env var and SDK `verify` option so ops can point to a known-good bundle or a custom SSLContext. Medium-term: publish Windows wheels for all supported Python versions (3.8-3.12) so users don't build against random system libs. Long-term: include a small TLS integration test in CI that runs on windows-latest for 3.8 and 3.11.

erin: We should also document known Windows quirks in DevEx docs (cert bundles, schannel vs openssl, proxies). And add a sample in examples/windows showing how to set REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE and how to pass an `ssl.SSLContext` into the client. Example snippet for passing context:

```
import ssl
from redwood import RedwoodClient
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='C:/certs/full-bundle.pem')
client = RedwoodClient(api_key='...', verify=ctx)  # new verify param accepts path/bool/SSLContext
```

marta: Also flag: typing/async parity. Users on Windows trying to use the async client are hitting type errors because we haven't shipped proper stubs for the async client and some Windows editors (PyCharm) struggle without wheels. We should add mypy in CI against the examples directory and include pyright checks for the async client.

devex-bot: Created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/523 
Title: "Add verify param + REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE support, docs, and Windows CI matrix" (WIP)

joel: Thanks 10 I'll try the verify=ctx approach in staging tomorrow. Any plan on how long we'll keep supporting 3.8? Ops still has a few services on 3.8 and customers ask about it.

marta: We officially support 3.8-3.12 for the next 12 months. We'll keep backports for critical fixes but will push users to upgrade. That said, wheels for 3.8 on Windows are low-effort and buy us a lot of reliability.

ci-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/issues/513 
"Windows TLS negotiation + typing/async parity on py3.8-3.12" labels: platform-windows, compatibility, enhancement. Assigned to @marta.

marta: Owners & next steps: 
- implement `verify` param accepting bool/str/ssl.SSLContext + REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE env var (marta)
- add windows-latest jobs for py3.8 and py3.11 with a TLS smoke test (alex to own CI config)
- publish DevEx doc + Windows troubleshooting guide (erin)
- add mypy/pyright checks for examples and async client stubs (devex team)

joel: Great. I'll report back after trying the SSLContext workaround in staging. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
